reason: The cited evidence (E1) shows that a poor ML force field can still yield an accurate phase diagram when end-member free energies are corrected with DFT, supporting the premise that periodic ab initio corrections can compensate for classical potential inaccuracies. However, E1 addresses a binary system and does not demonstrate the full multi-fidelity workflow, on-the-fly ML interpolation, or the claimed speedup and error bounds for multicomponent HEAs, leaving most key premises unsupported.
premises: Classical MD with a validated potential can broadly sample configurational space for multicomponent HEAs at low cost.
Periodic ab initio MD snapshots can provide high-fidelity energy corrections to the classical sampling.
An ML interpolation model can be trained on-the-fly to correct classical free energy estimates.
This multi-fidelity approach can capture vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron-vibration coupling.
The workflow can achieve <10% error in free energies and >10x speedup over full AIMD/TOR-TILD.
